The Reserve Fund's own 16 Sept 2008 announcement (“A Statement Regarding The Primary Fund”), retrieved via Wayback Machine (live reservefunds.com is defunct). Discloses $785M face value of Lehman debt written to zero and resulting Primary Fund NAV of $0.97/share effective 4:00PM ET, plus the $1.00 redemption cutoff at 3:00PM that day. Source for figures.json entries (c) and (e).

Fund press release dated 17 Sept 2008 restating Primary Fund NAV = $0.97 'as of 5:00pm ET on September 16, 2008' (note: differs from the 16 Sept release's own 4:00PM framing -- reported as an internal inconsistency, not resolved). Also gives Reserve Yield Plus Fund ($0.97) and Reserve International Liquidity Fund Ltd. ($0.91) NAVs.

Fund press release dated 22 Sept 2008 listing $1.00 NAVs for the fund's other (non-Primary) money-market series as of 19 Sept 2008; Primary Fund and Yield Plus funds marked 'Not available'. Background/context only, not a source for any of the five requested figures.

Fund press release dated 17 Sept 2008 stating the Reserve Insured Deposits and Cash Sweep bank-deposit programs (separate from the Primary Fund) were unaffected by the NAV break. Background/context only.
Fund press release dated 22 Sept 2008 announcing the SEC's order suspending redemptions from the Primary and U.S. Government Funds. Background/context only.

SEC Investment Company Act Release No. 28386 (22 Sept 2008): the SEC order temporarily suspending redemptions from the Primary Fund and U.S. Government Fund under Section 22(e)(3), as re-hosted on the fund's own site (sec.gov itself was not directly fetchable for this document -- see gap notes). Background/context only.
Fund press release dated 23 Sept 2008 clarifying the purpose of the SEC's 22 Sept redemption-suspension order. Background/context only.

Wayback snapshot (crawled 19 Sept 2008) of the fund's press/news-coverage listing page. Confirms www.reservefunds.com as the fund's genuine historical domain and links contemporaneous NYT/press coverage. No net-asset or NAV figures found on this page; used for domain confirmation and context only.

Wayback snapshot (crawled 27 Sept 2008) of the fund's press-release index by date, 16-26 Sept 2008. Used to enumerate and date the crisis-period PDF releases fetched alongside it (titles + dates only, no dollar figures on the page itself).
Fund press release dated 19 Sept 2008 listing $1.00 NAVs for other (non-Primary) Reserve money-market series as of 17-18 Sept 2008. Background/context only.

Fund press release dated 19 Sept 2008 announcing the SEC redemption-suspension application. Discloses Primary Fund AUM 'approximately $62 billion ... at the opening of business on September 15, 2008' and 'redemption requests this week of approximately $60 billion'; also gives the same pair of figures for the U.S. Government Fund ($10B AUM / $6B redemptions, not one of the requested figures). Corroborating source for figures.json entry (b).

Fund press release dated 18 Sept 2008: suspends new share purchases fund-wide and sets once-daily pricing times/cutoffs (Primary Fund 5:00pm ET) plus the 7-day redemption-proceeds delay policy. Background/context only.

Wayback snapshot of the SEC's own litigation-release index page. Live www.sec.gov blocked all direct fetch attempts (403 'Request Rate Threshold Exceeded' / 'Undeclared Automated Tool' -- see gap notes); this Wayback copy was used instead to discover that SEC v. Reserve Management Company is Litigation Release No. 21025 (5 May 2009) and to obtain the exact complaint PDF URL.

SEC Litigation Release No. 21025 (5 May 2009): announces the enforcement action SEC v. Reserve Management Company, Inc., Resrv Partners, Inc., Bruce Bent Sr. and Bruce Bent II, Civil Action No. 09-CV-4346 (S.D.N.Y.). Corroborates the $785M Lehman face-value figure (c) and gives the case caption / civil action number cited throughout figures.json.

SEC v. Reserve Management Company, Inc., et al. -- the actual 45-page civil complaint, Civil Action No. 09-CV-4346 (S.D.N.Y.), filed 5 May 2009. Primary source for figures.json entries (a-related) [RMCI-wide $120B AUM, Sept 12 2008, p.8], (b) [Primary Fund $62.4B total assets, morning of Sept 15 2008, p.17], and (d) [$10.7B of $24.6B redemption requests paid by 9am Sept 16 2008, p.33]; corroborates (c) [$785M Lehman face value, pp.2/17/22] and (e) [4:00pm ET NAV-break time, p.3]. Retrieved via Wayback Machine; live sec.gov blocked direct fetch of this same document (403 'Undeclared Automated Tool').

Matter of James v. iFinex Inc., 185 A.D.3d 22, 127 N.Y.S.3d 456, 2020 NY Slip Op 03880 (App. Div., 1st Dept, decided 2020-07-09; Gesmer, J.), same docket 450545/19 as the already-frozen 2019.04.24_signed_order.pdf. Located via CourtListener REST v4 search API (https://www.courtlistener.com/api/rest/v4/search/?q=iFinex+Letitia+James+450545+2019), which resolved to CourtListener opinion cluster 4766776 / docket 17334853; full text fetched directly from the official NY courts.state.ny.us slip-opinion mirror (courtlistener opinion-text endpoint returned 401 without an API key). NOT the Hoegner affirmation itself (that remains an open INSTRUMENT GAP -- see disclosure_passage_n1cretry.json) but IS a court document from the same matter that verbatim restates Tether's post-2019-03-04 change of representation: reserves include 'unspecified currency, "cash equivalents," and "other assets and receivables from loans made by Tether [Holdings] to third parties' -- no percentage figure. Confirms procedural fact: 'On or about April 30, 2019, respondents moved to modify or vacate the ex parte order.'

NYAG press release full body text (dated on-page April 25, 2019), fetched live 200 OK -- distinct from the already-frozen 2019.04.24_signed_order.pdf, which this page links to but does not itself contain. Contains 3 distinct dollar figures attributed to "the filings": $850 million (alleged Crypto Capital impairment/loss, quoted twice), $900 million (ceiling of Bitfinex's self-granted access to Tether's cash reserves), $700 million (amount Bitfinex had already drawn). See data/n1/tether2019/disclosure_passages_nyag.json for all 4 verbatim passages with exact wording. Does NOT contain the underlying Brian M. Whitehurst affirmation, petition, or memorandum of law that the signed order cites as its basis -- an exhaustive domain-wide Wayback CDX sweep of ag.ny.gov (2019-04-24..2019-05-31, 5375 rows) plus 3 filename-plausible sites/default/files/*.pdf candidates (checked via pdfplumber text extraction: complaint_as-filed.pdf = unrelated 2018 DOL case; petition_-_filed.pdf = image-only PDF with CreationDate 2018-01-16, predates this case; court_stamped_petition.pdf = 0 keyword hits in 81,063 extracted chars) found no such standalone document -- booked as an INSTRUMENT GAP in disclosure_passages_nyag.json. Feeds candidate phi-input (a) numerator: dollar impairment (three candidate figures, not resolved to one here).

Contemporaneous replacement source for PSMSOURCE (paper/fc27/fc27.tex Appendix B), freezing a dated public figure for the MakerDAO PSM's USDC balance on/about 2023-03-11, superseding the stale Jan-2023 ~$2.4B reporting figure previously in dai_backing.json. The Block, "USDC remains at about $0.90 following Circle's disclosure of funds at SVB" by Tim Copeland and James Hunt, published 2023-03-11T05:10:40-05:00 (10:10:40 UTC), Wayback-captured 2023-03-11T10:54:27Z (44 min after publication). Verbatim: "The stablecoin is about 36% backed by USDC, according to daistats. During the depegging events, some traders used their USDC as collateral to generate DAI, through its peg stability module. This has now reached its cap of 3.1 billion USDC, so no more DAI can be minted with USDC." Found via Wayback CDX domain sweep of www.theblock.co filtered to MakerDAO/DAI-titled URLs, 2023-03-08..2023-03-15 window, after daistats.com and makerburn.com (both client-side SPAs whose Wayback captures hold no embedded data) and forum.makerdao.com (governance threads, no balance figure) failed to yield a usable figure -- see data/n1/dai_psm_2023/cdx_search_log.json for the full query log and data/n1/dai_psm_2023/psm_source_20230311.json for the extracted figures. The $3.1B figure is a PSM-USDC-A debt-ceiling ('line') reading, not a custody reading, and differs materially from the existing $2.4B (Jan-2023) figure; the on-chain fields in dai_backing.json (block, dai_total_supply, on-chain PSM custody) are unchanged, since those are deterministic historical eth_call results already correctly frozen and do not require ETHERSCAN_API_KEY to re-verify. NOTE, UNRESOLVED (see constants.py): an earlier revision of this note asserted the $3.1B figure reconciled with the on-chain PSM balance via a 'refilled during the panic' story -- that reconciliation was wrong and is retracted; PSM sellGem transfers USDC INTO the join, so it cannot explain a ~$99 on-chain balance at the same block. Whether $3.1B was `line`, `Art`, or both is unresolved.
